Teacher Portal
User Manual

How to use the Teacher Portal on the web and on Android: sign in, take the register, record fee payments, review leave from home, report incidents, write behaviour logs, mark activities and participation, choose the Star of the Week, follow your class’s daily checklist, and teach from Let’s Learn Islam and the Madani Qaeda. One portal serves both of our madrasas, in Peterborough and in Manchester.

1. Before you begin

The Teacher Portal is where teachers run the day-to-day work of their classes: the register, fee payments handed in at class, leave requests from home, incident reports and behaviour logs, activities and participation marks, and the Star of the Week. It also holds your teaching books and the Let’s Learn Islam lessons. You only see students in the classes the office has assigned to you.

The madrasa office creates your account. Sign in with the email address on your teacher record. The password is the one you chose from the invite email, or the one you set after a reset. There is no public registration.

This manual online: /guides/teacher-portal-manual/

Our two branches

Nagina Social Welfare UK runs two madrasas. Your account belongs to one of them. After you sign in, the header, Dashboard and every list show your own branch and its students. There is nothing to choose at sign-in, and you never see the other branch’s records.

2. The Android apps

Android · available now

NSW Admin Portal

On an Android phone, install NSW Admin Portal from Google Play. It is the office app, published for admins and teachers. Open it, choose Teacher, and sign in with the email and password from the office. You cannot create an account from the store page.

Open the Play Store page
Android · coming soon

NSW Teacher Portal

An app just for teachers is ready and is being published to Google Play by Nagina Developer for Nagina Social Welfare UK. It opens straight to the teacher sign-in. When it is live, the office will send the link, and this manual will be updated with it.

There is no iPhone app yet. On an iPhone, add the web portal to your Home Screen (chapter 3).

The pictures in this chapter come from the NSW Teacher Portal app. After you choose Teacher in the NSW Admin Portal app, the pages are the same. Everything in them also works in the web portal.

Sign in

  1. Open the app from the home screen.
  2. Type your email and password. The eye icon shows or hides the password.
  3. Remember me is ticked already. Leave it ticked on your own phone, and the app opens straight to the Dashboard next time. Untick it on a shared phone.
  4. Tap Sign in. Forgot password? sends the same reset link as the web portal.

Home, Register, Leave, and Fees

A bar along the bottom holds Home, Register, Leave, Fees, and a grid button for every other page. A red number on Leave shows how many requests are waiting. Home is the Dashboard (chapter 6). Register, Leave and Fees are the same pages as chapters 8, 9 and 7.

The menu

The grid button at the right of the bottom bar, or the three lines at the top left, opens the menu. It lists every page: Dashboard, Receive Fee, Mark Attendance, Leave Requests, Incident & Behaviour, Activities, Participation, Star of the Week, My Profile, Teaching Resources, and Daily Checklist. Logout is at the top right of every page.

3. Open the web portal like an app

On any phone or computer, the teacher web portal can sit on your home screen or in the Dock. It opens in its own window, without the usual browser tabs. Use the same address and the same sign-in. The icon is labelled Markaz Admin. This is the way to use the portal on an iPhone.

Chrome on a computer

  1. Open Chrome and go to https://admin.naginasocialwelfare.co.uk/login/teacher.
  2. At the right of the address bar, click the install icon (a small screen with an arrow), then Install.
  3. If that icon is missing, click the three-dot menu, then Cast, save, and share, then Install page as app.
  4. The portal opens in its own window. You can also open it later from the Dock or the Start menu.

Chrome on Android

  1. Open the teacher web portal in Chrome.
  2. Tap the three-dot menu at the top right.
  3. Tap Install app. If you only see Add to Home screen, tap that instead.
  4. Confirm. The Markaz Admin icon appears on the home screen.

Safari on iPhone

  1. Open the teacher web portal in Safari. Other browsers on iPhone do not offer Add to Home Screen in the same way.
  2. Tap the Share button (the square with an arrow).
  3. Scroll the share sheet and tap Add to Home Screen.
  4. The name shown is Markaz Admin. Tap Add.
  5. Open the new icon from the Home Screen and sign in.

Safari on a Mac

  1. Open the teacher web portal in Safari.
  2. In the menu bar, choose File, then Add to Dock.
  3. Click Add.
  4. Open Markaz Admin from the Dock. It uses a simple window, without Safari’s full toolbar.

4. Open the web portal

The first screen asks you to choose a portal. Teachers use the green Teacher card. The other cards are for admins, parents, students, collectors, Islamic quizzes, and the Halal barcode helper.

  1. Open https://admin.naginasocialwelfare.co.uk
  2. On the Teacher card, press Continue.
  3. You land on the teacher sign-in page. You can also go straight there at https://admin.naginasocialwelfare.co.uk/login/teacher.

5. Sign in

The Teacher Sign In card asks for your email and password. Remember me is ticked already and keeps you signed in on this browser. Untick it on a shared computer.

  1. Type your email address.
  2. Type your password. The eye icon shows or hides it.
  3. Press Sign in.
  4. The Dashboard opens, with your name and your assigned classes.

A wrong email or password shows an error. Check the email with the office before trying again and again. If the office has switched your account off, sign-in does not work until it is switched on again.

After you are in, the menu down the left side is Dashboard, Receive Fee, Mark Attendance, Leave Requests, Incident & Behaviour, Activities, Participation, Star of the Week, My Profile, Teaching Resources, and Daily Checklist. Logout is at the top right and ends the session on this browser.

Forgot password

On the sign-in page, press Forgot password?. Enter the email on your teacher record, then Send link. Open the email and follow the link to choose a new password. Use Cancel if you opened the box by mistake.

First-time invite

When the office creates your account, you receive an email with a setup link. Open that full link. It opens a page titled “Set up your teacher account,” where you choose a password. After that you go to the Dashboard. The same password works in both Android apps.

If the link is incomplete, the page says Invite link incomplete. Use the whole link from the email, or ask the office to send a new invitation.

6. Dashboard

The Dashboard is your day at a glance. The header shows your branch, today’s date, and your name.

  • Welcome. A greeting, your assigned classes, how many registers are done today, and how many leave requests are waiting. Take register opens Mark Attendance.
  • Today. The Today’s register card shows each of your classes as Not marked yet or Done. Tap a class to open its register. Beside it are Pending leave, Registers done, and Students still to mark today.
  • Your classroom. Tiles for Receive Fee, Activities, Participation, Leave Requests, Incident & Behaviour, and Star of the Week. The Leave Requests tile shows how many are pending.
  • Tools. Teaching Resources, Islamic Quiz, and Halal Barcode.

Quran Academy, Manchester

A teacher at Quran Academy sees the same Dashboard with Quran Academy in the header and their own Manchester classes. Fees, registers, leave, reports and stars all stay inside the Manchester branch. Everything else in this manual works the same way.

7. Receive Fee

Receive Fee records money a family hands to you for a student in your classes.

  1. Open Receive Fee from the menu or the Dashboard tile.
  2. Under Who is paying, choose the Class and then the Student. The student card shows the parent’s contact number.
  3. Check the Month and Year. Fee due and Outstanding show what is owed.
  4. Type the Amount paid, or tap a quick amount: Fee due, Clear outstanding, £10, £20, or £50.
  5. Press Record Payment only when you have the money. Leave the page if you opened it by mistake.

A payment larger than one month fills the oldest unpaid month first, then future months in advance. The family sees the payment in the Parent Portal.

8. Mark Attendance

Mark Attendance is the daily register. It opens on today for your class.

  1. Open Mark Attendance, or press Take register on the Dashboard.
  2. To mark another day, tap it in the week strip or press Change. Open the filter row to pick a different class or search for a student.
  3. For each student, choose Present, Late, Absent, or Informed. Informed means the family told the madrasa in advance.
  4. Leave Uniform OK and Behaviour OK ticked, or untick them for that day.
  5. Give Extra stars (0, 1, or 2) for a really good day. They count towards Star of the Week.
  6. Press Save Attendance when the register is ready. Leaving without saving keeps the earlier marks.

The totals at the top count Present, Late, and Absent as you go. The calendar icon on a student row records a planned absence across a range of dates. View fees appears when a student owes money. A student shown as Student Blocked cannot be marked until the family clears overdue fees with the office.

9. Leave Requests

Parents, and students with a portal login, ask for leave from home. Requests for students in your classes come to you.

  1. Open Leave Requests. A red number in the menu shows how many are waiting.
  2. Switch between Pending, Reviewed, and All.
  3. Each request shows the student, class, dates, who sent it, and the reason.
  4. Press Approve or Reject. When rejecting, you can add a note for the parent.

Approving marks every day of the leave as Informed on the register for you. The family sees the decision in their portal.

10. Incident & Behaviour

This page has two tabs: Incident & Accident Report and Student Behaviour.

Incident & Accident Report

Use this for accidents, injuries, near misses, illness, behaviour that escalates, damage to the building, and safeguarding concerns. Submitted reports are listed on the left. Search by child, nature or place, and choose a report to read it on the right.

Press New report to open the form. It must be filled in within 24 hours, with facts only. The form has eight parts:

  1. Reporter details: your name, role, and when you are reporting.
  2. Incident overview: the date, time, location, and nature of the incident.
  3. Person(s) involved. Add another person adds more.
  4. Factual narrative and the immediate actions taken.
  5. First aid and medical response.
  6. Parent or guardian notification.
  7. Safeguarding and child protection, if it applies.
  8. Sign-off and verification.

Press Submit incident report only when it is complete. Cancel at the top closes the form without saving.

Student Behaviour

Student Behaviour is a short daily log for each student. Choose a student from the list, or search by student or parent name.

  1. Choose Good (a positive day) or Needs attention (worth a follow-up).
  2. Add a short note.
  3. Press Save Log.

Recent Logs lists earlier entries. Previous and Next move through the class, and Whole class goes back to the list. Notes you save appear in Madrasa life in the Parent and Student Portals.

11. Activities

Activities records each student’s progress through the class curriculum. The categories are Qaida, Quran, Surahs, Duas & Aqaaid, Islamic Education, and Participation, with the items the office has added for your class.

  1. Check the Date. Press Change to mark another day.
  2. Class focus shows how much of the class has been marked today. Choose a student from the list.
  3. Open a category, for example Qaida.
  4. For each item, choose Pending, Learning / In-Progress, Completed, or Not Completed.
  5. Back to Activities returns to the categories. Previous and Next move to the next student.

Request Next Activity asks the office to add the next curriculum item for a student. Request to remove asks the office to take a category off. Marks appear on the Learning page in the Parent and Student Portals.

12. Participation

Participation is for speeches, talks, nasheeds and other extra activities. It works like Activities: check the date, choose a student, open Participation, and mark each item the office has added for your class. If the class has no participation items yet, the page says so. Ask the office to add them in Curriculum.

13. Star of the Week

Each week, the child with the most stars in your class becomes Star of the Week. Stars come from attendance, uniform, behaviour, activities, participation, and the extra stars you give on the register.

  1. Open Star of the Week. It shows the current week. The arrows move to the previous or next week. Month and All years show longer periods.
  2. The list is sorted by total stars, with each child’s stars by type. The top child is the Auto pick.
  3. Keep the auto pick, or choose another child. Add an Override note to say why.
  4. Press Save selection to keep your choice. Press Finalize week only when the week is over.

14. Daily Checklist

Students tick a daily checklist of 20 good habits through the day, from waking up with salam to the dua before sleep. This page shows your class’s progress for one day. Each row shows a student, how many items they have done, and the behaviour rating for the day.

Press the date to look at another day. View month opens one student’s month. Use the page controls at the bottom for a large class.

15. Teaching Resources

Teaching Resources has two tabs: Let’s Learn Islam and Teaching Material.

Let’s Learn Islam

This tab shows every published Let’s Learn Islam module, whichever class it is assigned to. Use it to teach a lesson to the class. Nothing you do here is saved to any student’s progress.

  • English or اردو. Switches the lessons between English and Urdu.
  • Search and Filters. Search by title or topic, filter by class, or show only modules that have check questions.
  • Modules. Grouped by track, for example Fundamentals. Each card shows the lessons, cards, classes, and check questions.

Open a lesson to go through its cards one at a time. Show answer reveals the answer on a question card. Previous and Next move between cards. Present fills the screen for a projector or a big screen in class. All modules goes back to the list.

Teaching Material

Teaching Material holds the books and guides for your teaching, such as the complete Madani Qaeda and the Articulation Points of the Letters (Makhraj). Open reads a document inside the portal, page by page. Download PDF saves a copy to use offline. Teach in Let’s Learn Islam opens the matching lessons. The office adds more documents over time.

16. My Profile

My Profile shows your name, email, assigned classes, and subject. The office manages your subject and classes.

  • Personal details. Correct your full name, phone, or email. You sign in with this email, so changing it needs your current password.
  • Password. Press Change password, type your current password, then the new one twice.
  • Browser alerts. Alert me on this device asks this browser for permission to show a notification. On iPhone, add the portal to your Home Screen first.

17. Islamic Quiz and Halal Barcode

The Tools row on the Dashboard opens two public helpers. They need no sign-in, so you can share them with your class.

  • Islamic Quiz. Timed quizzes. In Halal or Haram rounds you tap Halal or Haram before the clock runs out. Knowledge quizzes are multiple choice.
  • Halal Barcode. Look up a UK shop product by its barcode, a scan, or a photo of the pack. It reads crowd-sourced pack labels. It is a helper for teaching and checking labels. It is not a Halal certificate and does not replace HMC, HFA, or other certification bodies.

18. Web portal on a phone

On a narrow screen the left menu is replaced by a bar along the bottom, the same as the app: Home, Register, Leave, Fees, and the grid button for every other page. The three lines at the top left open the same menu. Cards and tiles stack so you do not have to slide sideways. Logout stays at the top right.
